 Al-Ahli Jeddah vs Al-Gharafa Prediction: Al-Ahli Jeddah to Pull Away From Al-Gharafa
 Finished 26/10/2026 16:00 AFC Champions League Al Ahli Jeddah vs Al Gharafa 26.10.2026 
 Anastasia Dudkina 26/10/2026 11:55 Statistics of the month: 165 172 6 48.1 % ROI:   -8.13 % Statistics Odds Bet Type Bookmaker Claim Bonus! Odds 1,60 Bet Type BTTS: Yes Bookmaker Bonus 100 € Bet now! Al-Ahli Jeddah vs Al-Gharafa: Prediction for the match on October 26, 2026
 Al-Ahli Jeddah, who beat Al Khaleej Saihat (4-1), will be keen to carry that momentum into Monday’s AFC Champions League Elite clash.
 Al-Gharafa have points to pursue on matchday three of the West league stage. With Merih Demiral among three confirmed absentees, we expect the hosts’ selection problems to complicate their push for maximum points. 
 Receive Your Welcome Bonus! Al-Ahli Jeddah: Form and statistics
 Al-Ahli Jeddah’s revival began from a (1-2) defeat at Mamelodi Sundowns in the FIFA Intercontinental Cup. They answered by running riot at Al-Fateh (4-0). The goals kept coming on the road, with Al-Wasl FC beaten (3-1) in the AFC Champions League Elite and Al-Fayha edged (3-2) in the Pro League. With that attacking touch carried into their latest home success, the hosts have good reason to trouble Al-Gharafa, although conceding against both Al-Wasl and Al-Fayha gives the visitors encouragement. 
 Al-Ahli Jeddah: Lineup
 Shoulder rehabilitation keeps Saleh Abu Al-Shamat out, with Nayef Masoud also unavailable through a foot-joint injury, narrowing Al-Ahli’s options for changes against Al-Gharafa. 
 Expected XI: Abdulrahman Al-Sanbi, Saeed Baattia, Mohammed Sulaiman, Roger Ibañez, Saad Yaslam Balobaid, Valentin Atangana Edoa, Artem Bondarenko, Eduard Spertsyan, Francisco Trincão, Ivan Toney, Firas Al-Buraikan
 Al-Gharafa: Form and statistics
 On the road, Al-Gharafa’s (2-3) defeat at Al Wakrah offers little reassurance ahead of the trip to Jeddah. They have since settled for a share of the spoils with Al-Rayyan SC (0-0) and, most recently, Al Ahli Doha (2-2), with the latter result exposing defensive concerns again. The guests need a tighter showing against Al-Ahli Jeddah. 
 Al-Gharafa: Lineup
 The projected 4-2-3-1 gives Adam Ounas a supporting attacking role, with Fabricio Díaz providing midfield balance against Al-Ahli Jeddah. Yacine Brahimi is expected behind Alaaeddin Mohamed Hassan, with continuity favoured from the latest XI. The guests can produce plenty of shots, although their inconsistent output means that attacking support offers no assurance of a clinical showing in Jeddah. 
 Expected XI: Khalifa Ababacar, Amro Surag, Seydou Sano, Damé Traoré, Saifeldeen Fadlalla, Ayoub Mohamed Al-Oui, Fabricio Díaz, Adam Ounas, Ismaël Bennacer, Yacine Brahimi, Alaaeddin Mohamed Hassan
 Al-Ahli Jeddah vs Al-Gharafa: Head-to-head statistics
 Al-Ahli Jeddah ran riot (4-0) in their latest meeting with Al-Gharafa on October 20, 2025, in the AFC Champions League Elite. With two wins and three draws from their last five meetings, the hosts have history on their side, leaving the guests needing to break a winless run against this opponent.

 Al-Ahli’s scoring run gives their attack the strongest claim on our money against an Al-Gharafa defence still struggling for consistency. I expect the hosts to keep that pressure on; Home Over 2.5 team goals is my opening selection, priced at 1.82 by 1xBet. 
 Al-Gharafa need their supporting attackers to exploit Al-Ahli’s depleted defensive options, which gives the guests a route onto the scoresheet. Their uneven finishing makes this the higher-risk add-on: I favour Away Odd/Even Odd at Betway’s 2.14, with lower confidence than the home goals selection. 
 Four successive wins for Al-Ahli contrast with four winless outings for Al-Gharafa, giving the hosts the stronger claim to maximum points. The visitors’ defensive concerns and Al-Ahli’s absences also encourage goals at both ends. I would pair the home win with Over 3.5 goals; Paripesa offers Home/Over 3.5 at 2.62. 
 Al-Ahli Jeddah vs Al-Gharafa match prediction, October 26, 2026
 A repeat clean-sheet victory is not where I would put my money with Al-Ahli's defensive options stretched. Their attacking momentum makes a 3-1 Al-Ahli Jeddah win my preference, with Toney's forward line better placed to decide this contest than the makeshift defence is to shut Al-Gharafa out.
 Demiral's absence gives the guests an opening against the projected Sulaiman–Ibañez partnership. Al-Gharafa's uneven finishing is the strongest concern for backing goals at both ends, because attacking support alone won't punish those gaps. Brahimi's expected role behind the striker nevertheless gives them a route to trouble that altered back line without matching the hosts goal for goal. I expect both teams to score—Yes—with Al-Ahli's selection problems making an away goal credible. The hosts' sustained scoring threat against Al-Gharafa's defensive uncertainty also points me towards over 3.25 Asian total goals. For the winning margin, I favour Al-Ahli Jeddah -1.25 on the Asian handicap: the guests can contribute a goal without keeping pace with Toney and company.
